unlisted_practices: Payers should develop clear criteria for determining coverage of radiology AI applications and apply them consistently in coverage decisions.

Payers should reimburse separately radiology AI applications that improve diagnostic performance or provide new diagnostic information, provided evidence shows the improvement leads to better outcomes from a societal standpoint.
Payers should consider separate payment for radiology AI applications without direct clinical outcome evidence when the anticipated clinical or economic benefits are meaningful and readily apparent.

Payers should define acceptable evidence standards for radiology AI, recognising that high-quality non-randomized real-world studies can substitute where randomized controlled trials are difficult or impossible.
Payers should define what constitutes a meaningful benefit, as opposed to a statistically significant improvement, and the minimum level of evidence required to support it.
Payers should streamline reimbursement processes so technology manufacturers can make direct reimbursement requests.
Payers and technology developers should engage in early discussions on evidence requirements based on target product profiles.
Payers should evaluate radiology AI applications within the context of their own healthcare systems, including budget impact, when deciding whether and how to pay.

screen.reason: This is a framework/commentary paper discussing reimbursement criteria and financial adoption incentives for AI applications in radiology.
